questions.prompt: What information must travel from a parent to each child?

choices.label: The value of the immediately previous visited node.
choices.feedback: A good node is compared with its own ancestors, not nodes from other branches.

choices.label: The largest value anywhere in the tree.
choices.feedback: A good node is compared with its own ancestors, not nodes from other branches.

choices.label: The largest value on that path so far.

questions.prompt: When should the current node count as good?

choices.label: When its value is smaller than the path maximum.
choices.feedback: Equal values qualify: no ancestor may have a value greater than the current node.

choices.label: Only when its value is strictly greater than the path maximum.
choices.feedback: Equal values qualify: no ancestor may have a value greater than the current node.

choices.label: When its value is at least the path maximum.
choices.feedback: Equal values qualify: no ancestor may have a value greater than the current node.

questions.prompt: What maximum should be passed to each child?

choices.label: One shared maximum updated by either subtree.
choices.feedback: Each child inherits the maximum along its own root-to-parent path. The sibling subtree must not affect it.

choices.label: The larger of the inherited maximum and this node’s value.
choices.feedback: Each child inherits the maximum along its own root-to-parent path. The sibling subtree must not affect it.

choices.label: This node’s value, even if an ancestor was larger.
